podcast.body: This song had two distinct versions, reflecting the band's evolving sound and image. The 1982 version from *Saints & Sinners* featured a blues influence, with David Coverdale sporting long brown hair and the band dressed in jeans and leather jackets. By 1987, the version on the *Whitesnake* album showcased Coverdale with blonde hair and the band in leather pants, with almost all traces of the blues "erased," replaced by a heavier sound influenced by Def Leppard. The 1987 version reached number one on the Billboard Top 40 in October 1987, significantly boosted by its MTV video featuring Tony Catane. "Here I go again, that is from White Snake's seventh album, simply titled White Snake. The sound is heavier, definitely reflects more of a death leopard influence than a muddy waters influence. It became an international smash hit, made it to number one on the Billboard Top 40 in October 1987 and was helped along immensely by MTV."
